name: Tumor of Cranial and Spinal Nerves

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Cranial and Spinal Nerve Tumors

criteria.description: Progressive focal neurological deficits corresponding to affected cranial or spinal nerve distribution
MRI or CT evidence of a mass lesion involving cranial or spinal nerves with characteristic features
Histological confirmation of nerve sheath tumor or other nerve-origin neoplasm
Electrophysiological studies showing nerve conduction abnormalities in affected nerves

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive neurological deficits with supportive imaging findings; histopathology recommended for definitive diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, radiology, and pathology.

laboratory: No specific laboratory biomarkers; routine blood tests usually normal
imaging: MRI showing well-defined enhancing mass along cranial or spinal nerves
CT scan may show bone remodeling or erosion adjacent to tumor
genetic: Mutations in NF2 gene in schwannomas associated with neurofibromatosis type 2
other: Histopathological confirmation via biopsy showing nerve sheath tumor characteristics
